actions.name: Base speed
actions.longDescription:
You gain your maximum movement to use as you please from race and other sources like class or talents.

Game grid is in squares/cubes. One square/cube = 5feet of space.
Everything takes into account squares not feet mostly.
Going diagonally will take 2 squares every two squares, but you can skip that part to play game less complicated.
If your movement is reduced by half it will be rounded up, so 5 squares in half equal 3 squares

actions.name: Difficult terrain
actions.longDescription:
Its hard terrain like sand, snow, mountain rocks, shallow water and so on.
This hard terrain will take one more square when trying to go through that square.

Abilities that lower tier of difficult terrain does not stack. You need to lower it by two tiers directly.

## Greater difficult terrain

Its the worst terrain to move like swamp, blizzard, quick sand, slime and so on
This hard terrain will take two more squares when trying to go through that square.

- Normal terrain - 1 square = 1 square of movement
- Difficult terrain - 1 square = 2 square of movement
- Very difficult terrain - 1 square = 3 square of movement

## Hazard terrain
Mostly combined with difficult or very difficult terrain.
It has its own mechanics like a trap.
Hazard terrain could be a quicksand, lava, river, crumbling stones, wet climbing stones and so on

Jumping into difficult terrain will trigger DC 10 acrobatics check to not fall prone.
Into greater difficult terrain DC will be 15.

actions.name: Swimming speed
actions.longDescription:
Normally swimming will cost you one more squares to move through square requiring it.
You can avoid movement penalty with swimming speed.
Swimming speed matters in every liquid terrain that lets you swim in it like water, acid, lava(mostly unlikely) and other

The costs of movement with and without swimming speed:
- Without swimming speed - Double squares needed
- With swimming speed - Normal movement + penalties of hard terrain

Dungeon master can make you roll on treacherous waters to make athletics or (if it makes sense) acrobatics check against going with the current.

If you submerge in water you will have status drenched.

actions.name: Climbing speed
actions.longDescription:
Normally climbing will cost you one more squares to move through square requiring it.
You can avoid movement penalty with climbing speed.
Climbing speed matters in every terrain that you want to climb into like tree, wall, rope chains and other similar.

The costs of movement with and without climbing speed:
Without climbing speed - Double cubes needed + penalties of hard terrain
With climbing speed - Normal movement + penalties of hard terrain

To climb you need both hands free.

Dungeon master can make you roll on treacherous terrain to make athletics or acrobatics check against falling.
If you do not have climbing speed dungeon master can force you to roll same as above , but on normal terrain.
The DC for acrobatics should be harder by 2-5 points in DC.

Grabbing the edge DC athletics check to not fall.
- **DC 10**: normal terrain
- **DC 15**: difficult terrain
- **DC 20**: very difficult terrain

actions.name: Hovering
actions.longDescription:
If you have hovering speed you don't get penalties for walking on hard terrain, and can hover on liquids and not touch them.
Hovering speed lets you be in air when you are {{prone}} and have {{flying speed}}.
Hovering speed does not stop normal falling and falling damage.

actions.name: Flying speed
actions.longDescription:
While having flying speed, your character can fly in air and similar gasses.
If while flying you get {{prone}}, you will fall unless you have {{hovering}} speed or other method to prevent that.

actions.name: Burrowing speed
actions.longDescription:
If you have burrowing speed you can dig tunnels in soft terrain like sand and dirt fast.
You will leave tunnel if it makes sense.
You need both hands free to burrow at full speed.
Having only one hand free for burrowing will drop burrowing speed by half (rounded up)

Burrowing speed takes double the squares needed.

actions.name: Spider climb speed
actions.longDescription:
If you have spider climb you have {{climbing speed}}, but in addition, you can move up, down, and across vertical surfaces and upside down along ceilings, while leaving your hands free.
It eliminates any check that will force a creature to fall other that terrain being slippery or you falling with rubble you walked on.
Slippery and wet terrain will force character to make acrobatics check (dm decides DC) If character fails it will fall.

actions.name: How to calculate movement
actions.longDescription:
## Max speed
Your highest speed is the maximum of distance your character can make.
If you have 4 squares of flying speed and 6 squares of walking speed you have maximum of 6 squares of distance to spend.
You can combine movements, but it cannot exceed maximum movement and maximum of specific speed.

You can:
Move 6 squares by walking speed = 6
or
Move 4 squares by walking speed then fly 2 squares by flying speed = 4+2=6
or
Move 2 squares by walking speed then fly 2 squares by flying speed then move 2 squares by walking speed = 2+2+2=6

So for example if you have 4 squares of flying speed you cannot fly more than 4 squares, but can spend other movement speed up to your maximum speed.

actions.name: Preserved speed
actions.longDescription:
Any speed that you didn't spend on your turn will still be there for you until you get new turn.
Some abilities need that resource for you to move.

When you roll for initiative you will have half of your speed preserved (rounded down)
If you are surprised you will not have it.

actions.name: Bonus speed
actions.longDescription:
Sometimes you will gain bonus speed like going downhill (with check not to fall) or you gain momentum with wind behind your back.

1 cube worth of movement is 2 in this terrain or situation.

actions.name: Jumping
actions.longDescription:
Your character can jump.
Running start, if you walk 2 cubes in straight line you will get better result to your jumping power.

## Jump chart

- STR 5 = 5 cubes worth of jump horizontally and half as much (rounded down) vertically with running start
- STR 4 = 4 cubes worth of jump horizontally and half as much (rounded down) vertically with running start
- STR 3 = 3 cubes worth of jump horizontally and half as much (rounded down) vertically with running start
- STR 2 = 2 cubes worth of jump horizontally and half as much (rounded down) vertically with running start
- STR 1 = 1 cube worth of jump horizontally and half as much (rounded down) vertically with running start
- STR 0 = 1 cube worth of jump horizontally and half as much (rounded down) vertically with running start
- STR -1 = -1 cube worth of jump horizontally and half as much (rounded down) vertically with running start
- STR -2 = -2 cube worth of jump horizontally and half as much (rounded down) vertically with running start

Note: All jump measurements without running start are halved (rounded down)

## Size rules
Take that jump measurement and multiply it by size:

- Tiny: 1/4 original base
- Small: 1/2 original base
- Medium: x0
- Large: x2
- Huge: x4
- Giant: x6
- Gargantuan: x8
- Colossus: x10
- Tytan: x12

actions.name: Movement token interaction
actions.longDescription:
## Ending turn on other token space
You cannot end your turn in other active token space.
If you somehow end up in other token space at the end of THAT turn you are forced out into nearest unoccupied space.
If there isn't one you will be forced to have squeeze status with the other token you share space.
To do that you have to be 2 sizes smaller.

## Going through token forcefully
To go through an active token you have to use {{Tumble through}} action or have that token be willing to let you go through.
Going through that token will make that space one tier higher in difficult terrain.
If you are two sizes smaller that token you go through you don't have that penalty.

actions.name: Attack
actions.longDescription:
## Basic information
Attack action uses main action to allow you to gain strikes in this turn ( named differently to avoid confusion)
You gain as many strikes as your character allows you to. Mostly you will get two strikes.

## Strike
You can perform strike with your weapon. Any natural weapon such as claws or your fist counts as a weapon to.
When you make strike you roll d20 and add dexterity plus other bonuses and penalties. To see if you hit and compare result to AC of target you try to hit. It goes like this:
For all strikes: 1d20 + Dex mod + proficiency bonus + other bonuses + penalties

## Damage from strike
If you hit with strike you roll for the damage it inflicts. It goes like this:
For melee strikes and thrown weapons: (damage dice of weapon you hit) + STR mod + other bonuses + penalties
For ranged strikes (damage dice of weapon you hit) + Halved DEX mod (rounded down) + other bonuses + penalties.
Finesse weapons will have alternative option to use the same formula as ranged strike to deal damage.

## Flanking
To flank a foe, you and your ally must be on opposite sides of the creature.
A line drawn between the center of your space and the center of your ally's space must pass through opposite sides or opposite corners of the foe's space.
Additionally, both you and the ally have to be able to act, so this creature cannot be for example {{petrified}}, {{unconscious}}, {{stunned}}, {{paralyzed}} etc.
If creature is flanked all creatures gain +2 to hit this creature and +2 to forcing athletics and acrobatics rolls against it.

## Critical hit
If you roll natural one on d20 dice you will always fail to hit a target.
If you roll a natural 20 on d20 dice you will always hit and get critical strike which deals 2x damage

actions.name: Grapple
actions.longDescription:
## Basic information
You spend one strike or main action to grapple a creature within your arm reach. To grapple a creature you need at least one hand free. When you grapple a creature it occupies one hand slot.
You can grapple creatures of one size larger than, but you have disadvantage on roll for every size increase after 1 size that is larger than you.
(Advanced)You can choose to also do a prevent action for free, but its limited to holding a hand, but you do the roll with disadvantage. Success applies grapple and prevent.

## Grapple roll
To grapple you need to roll (1d20 + athletics skill bonus + other bonuses and penalties) and compare result to the enemy roll (1d20+athletics or acrobatics skill bonus + other bonuses and penalties).
If enemy result will be equal or higher than yours you lose and nothing happens.
If you succeed you apply grappled status to that creature. Grappler can end that status using reaction or free action.

## Moving with grappled creatures
When calculating ONLY movement WITH this creature you have to apply to your bulk weight of a creature. In short they don't encumber you, but they weight.
Depending on movement apply dragging rule or use normal calculation if you carry a creature in air/on you.
You can reposition a creature you are grabbing by spending your movement:
You can spend 1 cube of your movement to move that creature in your arms reach or move with it not changing position of grappled token.

## Grappling on longer distance
When you grapple creature with reach greater than 1 cube creatures can target your arm like your body (unless it has special mechanic)

actions.name: Trip
actions.longDescription:
## Basic information
You spend one strike or main action to trip a creature and make it prone within your arm or weapon reach. You can trip creatures with your arm or with weapon that makes sense. (for example you cannot trip with sling)
You can trip creatures one size bigger than you, but you have disadvantage on roll for every size increase after 1 size that is larger than you.

## Trip roll
To trip you need to roll (1d20 + athletics skill bonus + other bonuses and penalties) and compare result to the creature roll (1d20 + athletics or acrobatics + other bonuses and penalties) . If enemy result will be equal or higher than yours you lose.
If you succeed you apply {{prone}} status to that creature.

actions.name: Push
actions.longDescription:
## Basic information
You spend one strike or main action to push a creature within your arm or weapon reach. You can trip creatures with your arm or with weapon that makes sense.
You can push creatures 1 size bigger than you, but you have disadvantage on roll for every size increase after 1 size that is larger than you.

## Pushing to the side
You can push creatures in any horizontal direction, but the roll is made with disadvantage.

## Push roll
You spend one strike or an action to push a creature within your arm reach.
You then roll (1d20 + athletics skill bonus + other bonuses and penalties) and compare result to the creature roll (1d20+athletics or acrobatics + other bonuses and penalties). If enemy result will be equal or higher than yours you lose.
If you succeed you push creature up to 1 square horizontally away from you or to you (if possible) (you can gain more pushing power with feats)

## Forcing your way
Push action can be used as battering ram against locked doors, windows, chests and such.
Dungeon master will set the DC for you to break in.
He even can make breaking in require more than 1 success if it makes sense.

actions.name: Escape
actions.longDescription:
## Basic information
You spend one strike or main action to attempt an escape from grabbed, immobilized or {{restrained}}

## Escape roll
To get yourself free from one restrain you have to use your athletics or acrobatics and compare it to enemy athletics check OR compare it to the DC of hazard such as rope. (Rope tie DC = 10+ survival skill bonus + other bonuses and penalties)
I enemy is grappling you it counts as {{grapple}} attempt for him. If enemy result will be equal or higher than yours you lose.
If you succeed you get free from that status/situation.

actions.name: Disarm
actions.longDescription:
## Basic information
You make one strike like normal (using {{attack}} action) or main action to try to disarm other creature holding item or a weapon and force creature to drop it., Alternatively you can disrupt their wellbeing giving penalties.
You can disarm with your hand or with weapon.
You can disarm creatures 1 size bigger than you, but you have disadvantage on roll for every size increase after 1 size that is larger than you.

## Disarm roll
You make strike against chosen creature as normal, but with with disadvantage. Using ranged weapon gives another disadvantage.
If you would hit this creature with that strike on its AC you succeed and can choose to disarm a weapon or disarm creature wellbeing
Succeeding on disarming a weapon will cause creature to drop it and it suffers half damage from weapon strike (rounded down)
Succeeding on disrupting a creature will cause creature to have {{disarmed}} status until the start of your next turn and creature suffers half damage from weapon strike. (rounded down)

If you fail nothing happens
Note: If you have additional damage that has its source outside a weapon like smite feat from caster feat table. It will not be halved.

actions.name: Steal
actions.longDescription:
## Basic information
You spend one strike or main action to steal object from the creature in your arms reach.
To do this action you need at least one hand free.

## Steal roll
To steal you have to make roll (1d20 + thievery skill bonus + bonuses and penalties) and compare result to the enemy (DC of 10 + perception skill bonus + bonuses and penalties)
If creature is aware it might get robbed or you are observed by it you have disadvantage for this roll.
If an object is heavy or big (dm discretion) you have disadvantage on the roll.
You can only steal objects from hand that are not tightly gripped, you have to disarm tightly gripped
Planting items (Advanced) Alternatively you can plant an item into someone belongings. It has to be small enough. All penalties above still apply
Failing will break stealth potentially starting initiative.

actions.name: Prevent
actions.longDescription:
## Basic information
When you are grappling a creature you can go one step further.
You spend one strike or main action to prevent body part functioning, like hold jaw, cover eyes or hold limb.
Required hands are listed in options section.
You can prevent creatures 1 size bigger than you, but you have disadvantage on roll for every size increase after 1 size that is larger than you.

## Prevent roll
To prevent you have to make roll (1d20 + athletics skill bonus + other bonuses and penalties ) and compare result to the enemy roll (1d20+athletics or acrobatic + other bonuses and penalties). If enemy result will be equal or higher than yours you lose.
When creature escapes your grapple it loses any prevention.

## Options
(Requires both hands) Jaw hold/Covered mouth : Creature cannot make bite, tongue or other strike using mouth. Creature is silenced and can only muffle speak. Using this feature on creature two size larger will not silence it.
(One hand can hold one limb) Hold hand/limb: Creature cannot use this arm/limb for anything. Prevents dual wield and other things that make sense like using two handed weapons etc. Creatures have advantage to {{disarm}} or {{steal}} things from this hand.
(Requires both hands)Cover eyes: Creature now cannot see and is {{blinded}}. Using this feature on creature one size larger will not blind it. if cyclops is the target and is the same size as you it will not work due to size of an eye.

## Additional information
You can prevent of maximum creature size of 2 size bigger (it cannot be increased)
You need to use both hands to prevent limb of creature 1 size bigger.

actions.name: Use item
actions.longDescription:
## Basic information
You spend main action to use item as described in item.

## Scrolls
To get more information on scrolls you have to read said scrolls and feat ""Use magic items"" from arkana table
Scrolls will use action from ""Casting time"" scroll spell.
Scrolls can have Spell strengthen stickers, if you cannot use them you can still use spell scroll. Stickers won't be used.

## Potions
You can drink potions and make some other willing creature drink it. You cannot make {{unconscious}} creature drink a potion, it will be wasted. You have to buy this potion in syringe or put it in there.
To administer syringe to unwilling creature you have use your normal strike (not this action) with syringe as improvised weapon and hit temporary or life hit points. Syringe have additional tags (light, finesse, concealable) and will deal 1d2 piercing damage

## Coat poisons
All poisons can be coated on weapons, but only slashing and piercing will do anything. You can coat with one poison one weapon with three charges or three ammunitions with one charge (bullet have to be specially made)
When this ammunition or weapon will hit a creature it will lose one charge of poison and if damage hit temporary or life hit points it will trigger its effect on that creature.
Coating will last until poison is removed.

## Hiding or Concealing item
You can use this action to hide trap or item in environment or on your belongings. Weapons with ""conceal"" tag can be hidden and benefit from Big cover bonus from clothes. (+5)
The DC to spot this said item/trap with perception is rolled (1d20 + thievery or survival ability bonus + other bonuses and penalties)
Passive perception can detect them.

actions.name: Ready
actions.longDescription:
## Basic information
You spend an action for it to be spend on specific reaction springed on moment described by you.
You can strike only one time when you do the {{Attack}} action.
Even if you meet requirements for reaction to spring, you don't need to do that reaction.

## Readying {{Dash}}
When you use ready action to use dash action you are not granted speed bonuses from dash action, instead you can use stored movement and move as you like, but once you move and stop the ready action is stopped.

actions.name: Dash
actions.longDescription:
## Basic information
When you take the Dash action, you gain extra movement for the current turn and gain one melee strike that will be made with double disadvantage and using it will end your whole movement.
The increase equals to your maximum speed.

## Bonus {{tumble through}} action
When you use dash action can also attempt one tumble through enemy creature space. (See tumble through action)

## Examples
With a speed of 6 squares, for example, you can move up to 12 squares on your turn if you dash.
Any increase or decrease to your speed changes this additional movement by the same amount. If your speed of 6 squares is reduced to 3 squares, for instance, you can move up to 6 squares this turn if you sprint.

actions.name: Dodge
actions.longDescription:
When you take the Dodge action, you focus entirely on avoiding.
Until the start of your next turn:
- Any strike made against you has disadvantage if you can precisely sense the striking creature.
- You make reflex saving throws with advantage.
- You have advantage on acrobatics skill rolls against contesting skill against athletics.
You lose this benefit if you cannot move or you are squeezed (squeeze rules)

actions.name: Disengage
actions.longDescription:
## Basic information
If you take the Disengage action, your movement doesn’t provoke {{opportunity strike}}s until the start of your next turn.

## Bonus {{tumble through}} action
When you use disengage action can also attempt one {{tumble through}} enemy creature space. (See tumble through action)

actions.name: Tumble through
actions.longDescription:
## Basic information
You spend one strike or main action to Tumble through an enemy space allowing you to pass.
To do that you need to roll 1d20 + Athletics/Acrobatics skill mod against enemy 1d20+athletics skill modifier.
If enemy result will be equal or higher than yours you lose and nothing happens.

## Going through tokens
All interactions with other creatures are in ""Movement token interaction"" in movement table

actions.name: Distract
actions.longDescription:
You use your main action or bonus action to distract enemies from something.
Specify targets of distraction, like you doing some stupid faces in front of guard or throwing rock at certain location. You can choose how much enemies you want to affect, but dm will decide that.
You then roll 1d20 + deception skill bonus and compare result to the enemy DC of 10 + perception/insight skill bonus (depending on nature of distraction)

Success: You successfully apply {{distracted}} status to the target specific for your action until your next end of turn.
Failure: Target of your distraction saw through your distraction or didn't bother with it.

actions.name: Hide
actions.longDescription:
When you take the Hide action, you try to not get observed and gain {{hidden}} status for creatures that have trouble sensing you.
Using visions, lightning, cover and distractions you can change from observed to noticed.
Cover gives bonuses to stealth.

You spend main action to try to hide.
You then roll 1d20+dex mod + stealth proficiency + other bonuses and penalties and compare it to passive perception of creatures you are able to hide against.
Hiding fails when in space of hiding you are still clearly seen/sensed.

actions.name: Seek
actions.longDescription:
You can attempt to seek to detect what is hidden from you with main action
You seek area with your chosen sense and roll a perception skill check.

actions.name: Dirty trick
actions.longDescription:
## Information
You can use dirty trick to do lots of stuff depending on your action.
It requires you to spend 1 interaction and 1 strike.
Here are options:

## Fakeout

You try to fake your action against an enemy that unprecisely senses you within 6 cubes. You need to roll deception skill roll vs enemy perception skill roll. If enemy roll is equal or higher than yours, you lose.
If you win you gain double advantage on next strike roll, athletics or dexterity skill roll you choose against that enemy until the start of your next turn.

## Disrupt sense

It has range of 1 cube, you describe what and how you want to disrupt one sense from one creature chosen.
Depending on your action creature has to make either reflex, fortitude or will saving throw on your class DC
If creature fails it will have targeted sense lowered by 1 tier until the end of your next turn.
If creature failed by 5 or more it has sense lowered by 2 tiers instead.

actions.name: Grab the edge
actions.longDescription:
## Basic information
When you fall near the edge or something that you can grab you can spend reaction or one strike action to save yourself from falling.
You need at least one hand free. Having only one hand free will make you roll with disadvantage.

## Grab the edge roll
To grab the edge you have to roll (1d20 + athletics or acrobatics skill bonus + other bonuses and penalties) and compare result to the terrain DC+number of cubes you fallen (information in movement table, climbing section)

- **Success by 5+ the DC:** You grab onto something and stop falling. You reduce (10+athletics/acrobatics ability bonus) worth of damage
- **Success:** You grab onto something and stop falling. You reduce (5+athletics/acrobatics ability bonus) worth of damage
- **Failure:** Nothing, you still fall

actions.name: Delay turn
actions.longDescription:
To do this action you have to be conscious and essentially, you can't Delay to avoid negative consequences that would happen on your turn or to extend beneficial effects that would end on your turn.
So for example if your character have {{lured}}, {{frenzied}} or {{hypnotized}} status, it cannot delay its turn.

You wait for the right moment to act. The rest of your turn doesn't happen yet.
Instead, you're removed from the initiative order.
You can return to the initiative order as a free action triggered by the end of any other creature's turn.
This permanently changes your initiative to the new position.
You can't use reactions until you return to the initiative order.
If you Delay an entire round without returning to the initiative order, the actions from the Delayed turn are lost, your initiative doesn't change, and your next turn occurs at your original position in the initiative order.
When you Delay, any negative effects that normally occur at the start or end of your turn occur immediately when you use the Delay action.
Any beneficial effects that would end at any point during your turn also end.
The GM might determine that other effects end when you Delay as well.

actions.name: Grab falling creature/item
actions.longDescription:
## Basic information

You can use reaction or main action to grab falling creature in your hands reach. It cannot be 2 sizes times larger than you. (size increase does not work) Creature/item needs to be in arms reach
Every creature size that is bigger than you by 1 gives disadvantage on roll. Works on big items to, you compare its size to creature size.
You need both hands free for creature and 1 hand free for small item.
Works on items dropped or that are harmlessly thrown, but not projectiles thrown to harm.

## Grab falling creature/item roll
To grab falling creature you have to roll (1d20 + athletics skill bonus + other bonuses and penalties) and compare result to the DC of (10 + 2xnumber of cubes target falls)

- **Critical success:** You grab creature/item and stop its fall. You reduce (10+athletics ability bonus) worth of damage
- **Success:** You grab creature/item and stop its fall. You reduce (5+athletics ability bonus) worth of damage
- **Failure:** You fail to catch creature/item.
- **Critical failure:** You fail to catch creature/item and you automatically fail saving throw against falling creature/item.

actions.name: Dispel magic
actions.longDescription:
**Requires: Access to mana or mana pool**

You use main action for this feature. It has range of a 6 cubes and requires precise sense.
You can target a creature, object or spell that you know about.
You then spend same amount of mana that the spell was created with and need to roll on arkana.
DC is 12+mana spend on spell that is going to be dispelled.
This ability can dispel also magical barriers that grant AC or other magical phenomena from NPC creatures.
The DC to dispel them is the AC of creature you target. You can target magic by being blinded when you have magic vision.

If you fail you lose 1 mana, you will lose 0 mana if spell was worth only 1 mana.

If you fail the check, mana used is refunded.

actions.name: Assist
actions.longDescription:
## Basic information
You spend main action to assist a creature within your arm reach and use one option below:

## Getting up creature
You can use half of your movement (rounded down) and lift willing creature from {{prone}} status using one hand. Bigger creatures require both hands. You can do this action to maximum creature 1 size bigger
(Size increase on athletics skill works) This does not trigger {{opportunity strike}}.
## Untie a creature
You can attempt to free a creature from restrains. Simple untying from rope or webbing of spiders. Attempt athletics or survival skill check against DC of restrain, grab or other similar status.
## Extinguish
You can try to extinguish a creature or item by using half of your movement (rounded down)
## Wake up
You can wake someone up from {{unconscious}} (asleep) condition.
## Help reach higher/further distance
You can help creature to get higher. (requires shield, free hand or weapon that makes sense) It boosts jump by your push distance (basically 1 cube)
## Snap out
You can trigger saving throw to get rid of {{hypnotized}}, {{controlled}}, {{confused}}
## Assist in battle
You can cause friendly (other than yourself) creature to make strike, athletics check or acrobatics check be made with advantage. You have to use assist action and specify you are going to assist, if creature performs a strike or athletics check against a creature within your melee weapon reach you can give advantage to a creature that tries to use this strike or athletics action. To give advantage on acrobatics check you have to have to have creature you want to assist within our weapon reach.

## Stabilization
You can stabilize only alive creatures.
You roll (1d20+medicine skill + other bonuses and penalties) and compare roll to the stabilization DC of a creature. (make recall knowledge on creature to know the DC) (DC is in races table or in monster statblock)
If you pass the creature is stable and will not need to roll death saving throws. Stable person will regain consciousness in 1 hour getting 1 life hit point..
If you fail nothing happens, If you fail by 5 points or more you give creature +1 wounded status potentially killing it.

## Administer potion
You can administer syringe potion into a willing creature . (just like use item action) (yourself included)
To administer syringe to unwilling creature you have use your normal strike (not this action) with syringe as improvised weapon and hit temporary or life hit points. Syringe have additional tags (light, finesse, concealable) and will deal 1d2 piercing damage

## Give air
You can give by mouth to mouth designated air from you into a creature lungs.

## Prevent {{bleeding}}
You roll (1d20+medicine skill + other bonuses and penalties) and compare roll to the DC of a bleeding. If result is equal or higher , bleeding will be removed
**Failure by -5 the DC** - creature receives bleed damage

## (Advanced) Treat disease
If you have appropriate proficiency to deal with disease you can spend 4 hours to care for 1 creature. Creature can make next disease saving throw with advantage.

- **Success by 5+ the DC** - Creature will make saving throw with double advantage
- **Success** - Disease status is 1 tier lowered
- **Failure by -5 the DC** - Disease status is 1 tier lowered

Other: If there is status that is important to treat with medicine you can use similar formula to the prevention of bleeding or treating disease.

## Helping with task
You can help in tasks that you are capable of helping, by dungeon master discretion this task can have DC lowered or consume less time.

actions.name: Latch on (Experimental)
actions.longDescription:
You spend one strike to {{grapple}} an creature within your arm reach.

You can hang on creatures that are 2 size larger than you and you need to spend half of your maximum movement (rounded down)
Willing creature does not require rolling.
You then roll 1d20 + athletics or acrobatics skill bonus and compare result to the enemy roll 1d20+athletics or acrobatics. If enemy result will be equal or higher than yours you lose.
If you succeed you climb onto a creature.
To hang on creature you have to have two hands free or have something to hang on to. (Climbing rules)
Now you move with that creature and can climb it.
Any climbing related feat and climbing speed will apply to this.
Your equipment and you will add bulk to the creature you hang onto.
Creature you hang on have disadvantage to strike you.
Getting off takes your half of maximum movement (rounded down)
Being {{grappled}} or {{restrained}} will get you off creature you hang on.

actions.name: Recall knowledge
actions.longDescription:
You can use action to think about what are you encountering. Based on how many hints you have you can have DC lowered or heightened by Dungeon master
When you are about to use recall knowledge dungeon master presents you with required skill for roll. Then you can decide if you want to attempt that action.
Every creature have in their statblock DC of that recall knowledge. Depending on roll dungeon master can give this creature information about their attacks, behaviours and so on or lie when silent roll is very bad.

actions.name: Throw creature
actions.longDescription:
## Basic information
To throw a creature you have to {{grapple}} it, have second hand free and it has to be the one same size lower than you. (any increase from feats works)
When you meet all requirements you can just throw a creature using one strike or main action.
Throw is not possible if creature exceeds your whole bulk limit.
Exceeding first stage of encumbrance decreases thrown distance by half.

## Distance (no roll required)
The distance of throwing a creature is 1 cube of movement per creature and equipment bulk times your ""free"" bulk space until second stage of encumbrance. Throwing a creature upwards costs 2x times more
You can throw a creature where you want.

actions.name: Distract
actions.longDescription:
You use your main action or bonus action to distract enemies from something.
Specify targets of distraction, like you doing some stupid faces in front of guard or throwing rock at certain location. You can choose how much enemies you want to affect, but dm will decide that.
You then roll 1d20 + deception skill bonus and compare result to the enemy DC of 10 + perception/insight skill bonus (depending on nature of distraction)

Success: You successfully apply {{distracted}} status to the target specific for your action until your next end of turn.
Failure: Target of your distraction saw through your distraction or didn't bother with it.

actions.name: Pointout
actions.longDescription:
You use an reaction and indicate a creature, object or illusion that you can precisely sense to creatures that unprecisely sense you, gesturing in a direction and describing the distance verbally.
You need to be able to communicate with desired creatures. If you all have special gestures it can work without speaking.
That creatures can use reaction to make seek action against pointed out creature, object , illusion etc. and everything in 2 cubes around it.
Any language barrier will give disadvantage on seek action.

actions.name: Grab the edge
actions.longDescription:
## Basic information
When you fall near the edge or something that you can grab you can spend reaction or one strike action to save yourself from falling.
You need at least one hand free. Having only one hand free will make you roll with disadvantage.

## Grab the edge roll
To grab the edge you have to roll (1d20 + athletics or acrobatics skill bonus + other bonuses and penalties) and compare result to the terrain DC+number of cubes you fallen (information in movement table, climbing section)

- **Success by 5+ the DC:** You grab onto something and stop falling. You reduce (10+athletics/acrobatics ability bonus) worth of damage
- **Success:** You grab onto something and stop falling. You reduce (5+athletics/acrobatics ability bonus) worth of damage
- **Failure:** Nothing, you still fall

actions.name: Hold breath
actions.longDescription:
## Basic information
You can use reaction to hold more breath than normally.
You can hold breath for (10 + Constitution mod) rounds.
Talking or casting spell with verbal component will take 2 rounds from total.

## Losing all rounds of breath
After that if you are unable to breathe you will fall unconscious and lose 10 life points every start of your turn that is bypassing shield points and temporary points.

actions.name: Grab falling creature/item
actions.longDescription:
## Basic information

You can use reaction or main action to grab falling creature in your hands reach. It cannot be 2 sizes times larger than you. (size increase does not work) Creature/item needs to be in arms reach
Every creature size that is bigger than you by 1 gives disadvantage on roll. Works on big items to, you compare its size to creature size.
You need both hands free for creature and 1 hand free for small item.
Works on items dropped or that are harmlessly thrown, but not projectiles thrown to harm.

## Grab falling creature/item roll
To grab falling creature you have to roll (1d20 + athletics skill bonus + other bonuses and penalties) and compare result to the DC of (10 + 2xnumber of cubes target falls)

- **Critical success:** You grab creature/item and stop its fall. You reduce (10+athletics ability bonus) worth of damage
- **Success:** You grab creature/item and stop its fall. You reduce (5+athletics ability bonus) worth of damage
- **Failure:** You fail to catch creature/item.
- **Critical failure:** You fail to catch creature/item and you automatically fail saving throw against falling creature/item.

actions.name: Opportunity strike
actions.longDescription:
Opportunity strike is always made with disadvantage and you have to precisely sense a creature or feel it (like grappling it).
Any bonus thing you do after successful opportunity strike is made with the same penalty.
You can only do this reaction using a melee weapon strike, thrown or ranged strike does not work.

You are granted to make opportunity strike after one of these things happened :

When enemy creature moves out of your reach of your weapon.
When enemy creature casts a spell within reach of your weapon.
When enemy makes a ranged strike within your reach of your weapon. This does not count for throwable weapon.
When enemy creature stands up from {{prone}} condition by itself within reach of your weapon.

actions.name: Raise shield
actions.longDescription:
When you have shield in hand you can spend reaction and use it to gain shield hit points equal to shield type (item) + proficiency in armor(+0, +1, +2 or +4) and other bonuses and penalties.
You also add one tier of cover against one strike if you use it when strike hits you or against reflex saving throw.

actions.name: Magical shield
actions.longDescription:
**Requires: Access to mana or mana pool**

You can use reaction to spend X mana to gain X*4 shield hit points.
X is the mana spend. You can use as much mana as you want.
You also add one tier of cover against one strike if you use it when strike hits you or against reflex saving throw.

actions.name: Calm beast creature
actions.longDescription:
## Commanding creatures
As a free action or reaction you can command a willing creature of what to do.
Trained creature does not need any check for simple tasks. Untrained creature however has trouble to understand and can do only simple task.
This rule can be used when creatures want to communicate with themselves not sharing a language, but you will use relevant skill to the situation.

Untrained creature simple task or Trained creature Complicated task DC = 2xnegative intelligence+8-positive intelligence if possible. on Nature or fitting lore skill.
Failing will block any interaction for you until the start of your turn. Feel free to add or reduce DC depending on situation.
Trained creatures WILL follow the last command if possible.

## Calm beast creature
If a creature is scared of place, or situation, but not completely hostile you can try to calm it. Example: Horse is scared of wolves and wants to run away.

The DC on nature is usually 10, but depending on situation dungeon master can increase or lower the DC.
If you succeed the creature is calmed until it is startled again. Failing will block any interaction for you until the start of your turn or even start a fight.

actions.name: Blinded
actions.longDescription:
A blinded creature have no sense of vision and will lose any vision like, heat vision, magic vision etc.

Creatures immune to blinded will still be blinded in heavy obscurement.

actions.name: Deafened
actions.longDescription:
A deafened creature will have no sense of hearing
Deafened creature will have 25% chance to fail any verbal sound or magic component wasting an appropriate action (not spellslots).

actions.name: Distracted
actions.longDescription:
Creature that is distracted will have disadvantage on all senses related rolls and insight out of specified target or area and 2 cubes around it.
Creature will not have any downside to its perception and insight within range of distraction.
Distracted creature needs to be able to observe distracting target or only notice it if its related to hearing sense. If it cannot do that, distracted status won't work.
Distraction can allow hiding in open space when outside space of focus.

This status is related to **psychic damage**

actions.name: Taunted
actions.longDescription:
Taunting creatures have special effects:
Disadvantage on strike rolls and forcing athletic rolls against all creatures except taunter.
Taunter have advantage against this creature saving throws and its spells.
Taunted creature needs to be able to observe taunting target or only notice it if its related to hearing sense. If it cannot do that, taunted status won't work.

This status is related to **psychic damage**

actions.name: Frenzied
actions.longDescription:
Frenzied creature is also {{Taunted}} even if its immune to that status.
A frenzied creature will have to harm or include creature that made it frenzied in area of effect that will directly harm it while in this status.
Frenzied creature needs to be able to observe target that gave it this status or only notice it if its related to hearing sense. If it cannot do that, Frenzied status won't work.

This status is related to **psychic damage**

actions.name: Poisoned
actions.longDescription:
A poisoned creature has disadvantage on everything except its own recovery rolls against this status.
Poisons have different effects depending of poison.
If poisoned gives other status it remains there unless poisoned status is removed.

actions.name: Restrained
actions.longDescription:
A restrained creature’s speed temporarily becomes 0, and it can’t benefit from any bonus to its speed.
Strike rolls against the creature have advantage and steal action against this creature is made with double advantage.
Creature is unable to perform somatic component for a spell and have disadvantage on strike rolls and athletics rolls
Creature have {{clumsy}} status.
Creature cannot block path by purpose.

actions.name: Grappled
actions.longDescription:
A grappled creature’s speed becomes 0, and it can’t benefit from any bonus to its speed.
The condition ends if the grappler is {{paralyzed}}, {{petrified}}, {{stunned}} or {{unconscious}}.
The condition also ends if an effect removes the grappled creature from the reach of the grappler or grappling effect, such as when a creature is hurled away by the thunderwave spell.

Weapons that grapple creatures on range can still walk to the source of grapple, including natural ones like hands.
If you are grappled by natural weapon like claw, you can strike directly the grappler.
Grappler can end that status using reaction or free action.

actions.name: Prone
actions.longDescription:
A prone creature’s only movement option is to crawl, unless it stands up and thereby ends the condition.
Crawling treats all terrain to be 1 tier higher in difficulty.
The creature has disadvantage on attack rolls and cannot use ranged weapons except blowgun, crossbow and pistols.
An strike roll against the creature has advantage if the attacker is within 2 cubes of the creature. Otherwise, the strike roll has disadvantage.
You cannot be prone in water.

You can stand up using half of your maximum movement (rounded down). If you have 0 cubes of movement you cannot stand up.

actions.name: Sickened
actions.longDescription:
A sickened creature has disadvantage on everything except its own recovery rolls against this status.
Diseases have different effects depending on disease.
If sickened gives other status it remains there unless sickened status is removed.
This status can stack.

This status is related to **decay damage**

actions.name: Unconscious
actions.longDescription:
An unconscious creature cant take any action, can’t move or speak, and is mostly unaware of its surroundings
The creature drops whatever it’s holding and falls prone.
The creature automatically fails any strength or dexterity related rolls
Strike rolls against the creature have advantage.
Creature have disadvantage on perception rolls
You gain {{Assailable}} status
You also don't take into account your dexterity when calculating AC

Asleep rule: If creature is unconscious due to the sleeping any damage or spending action touching it will wake it up.
It can be awake by loud noise with DC 5-14 perception roll based on hearing that can be rolled once per round. (dc may wary due to loudness)

actions.name: Overstimulated
actions.longDescription:
You have disadvantage on every perception check and sense related rolls
All senses are 1 tier lower.

This status is related to **psychic damage**

actions.name: Trembling
actions.longDescription:
A trembling creature has disadvantage on skill checks and attack rolls while the source of its status is within line of sense.
It means you need to have full cover and peeking/looking into this line of sight will activate effect of status.
The creature can’t willingly move closer to the source of its status.

actions.name: Frightened
actions.longDescription:
Creature that is frightened will have {{trembling}} status (even if you are immune to trembling status)
and can act normally only when its within a place out of line of sight of status source.
It means you need to have full cover and peeking/looking into this line of sight will activate effect of status.
Creature while frightened needs to do everything in its power to get out of line of sight of creature that made status to this creature.

actions.name: Charmed
actions.longDescription:
Charmed creature regards a creature that got it this status (charmer) a friend. If charmer will communicate what creatures are his friends it will work on them to.
Charmed creature cannot do anything that would be harmful to charmer and his ""friends""
Charisma rolls against a charmed creature by charmer are made with advantage.
Charmed creature will know it was charmed only after the end of a status.
If something harmful or heavily threatening from charmer or his ""friends"" is done to charmed creature it loses this status.

## Example
Charmer makes ready action to stab charmed creature
Charmer will threaten to burn charmed creature house and family

This status is related to **psychic damage**

actions.name: Hypnotized
actions.longDescription:
You cannot take any actions.
You fail any will and reflex saving throws.
You fail any skill roll against you.
You also don't take into account your dexterity when calculating AC
Every time creature gets damage can repeat saving throw if possible. Does not work on poisons.

This status is related to **psychic damage**

actions.name: Controlled
actions.longDescription:
Someone else is controlling you completely.
You need to hear or understand what a creature that is controlling you wants you to do.
You do the task until its done or status is gone.
Every time creature gets damage can repeat saving throw if possible. Does not work on poisons.

This status is related to **psychic damage**

actions.name: Lured
actions.longDescription:
A creature that is lured needs to spend all its resources to get as close as it can to the source of luring.
Creature will take shortest route getting itself at risk.
Creature can act normally only when is adjacent to a source of luring.
Every time creature gets damage can repeat saving throw if possible. Does not work on poisons.
If creature have multiple sources of luring, it prioritizes the closest source.

This status is related to **psychic damage**

actions.name: Dazzled
actions.longDescription:
Dazzled creature have 25% chance at start of a turn to speak only gibberish failing any verbal communication or order. Also it fails to understand others.
Strike rolls against the creature have advantage, and the creature’s strike rolls have disadvantage.
Creature have disadvantage on perception rolls.
If you get dazzled status on top of existing one it changes to {{stunned}} status and you lose dazzled status

Status is related to **sonic damage**

actions.name: Stunned
actions.longDescription:
Stunned overrides {{dazzled}}
A stunned creature cant take any action, can’t move, and can speak only gibberish failing any verbal communication or order.
The creature automatically fails any strength or dexterity related rolls
Strike rolls against the creature have advantage.
Creature fails to understand others and have disadvantage on perception rolls.
You gain {{Assailable}} status
When you lose {{stunned}} status you will get dazzled status
You also don't take into account your dexterity when calculating AC

Status is related to **sonic damage**

actions.name: Petrified
actions.longDescription:
You cannot take any actions.
A petrified creature is transformed, into a solid inanimate substance (usually stone).
Its weight increases by a factor of ten, and it ceases aging.
Strike rolls against you are made with advantage
The creature automatically fails any saving throws except will.
Creature is {{restrained}}
The creature gains resistance 7 to all damage (except sonic and death).
It gains vulnerability 5 to sonic damage and immunity to death damage.
The creature is immune to poison and disease, although a poison or disease already in its system is suspended, not neutralized.

## Turning into stone
While petrification is in motion you will be {{clumsy}} for the whole process.
Now you need to count fails. At the end of a turn you will have to repeat saving throw. Succeeding DC will remove one fail from count.
If you fail again (Second fail) you gain {{restrained}} status and you have disadvantage against being tripped.
You can also spend whole action to damage yourself with slashing weapon to cut off your legs to immediately free yourself, but you lose legs.... (half movement for crawling)
On the third fail you cannot use your hands.
On the final fourth fail you are petrified.

actions.name: Numb
actions.longDescription:
Numb creature can use either main action or bonus action.
You have {{clumsy}} status

If you get numb status on top of existing one it changes to {{paralyzed}} status and you lose numb status
This status is related to **electric damage** unless it comes from poison.

actions.name: Paralyzed
actions.longDescription:
Paralyze overrides {{Numb}}
A paralyzed creature cant take any action and can’t move or speak.
The creature automatically fails any strength or dexterity related rolls
Attack rolls against the creature have advantage.
You gain {{Assailable}} status
When you lose paralyzed status you will get {{numb}} status
You also don't take into account your dexterity when calculating AC

This status is related to **electric damage** unless it comes from poison.

actions.name: Invisible
actions.longDescription:
You cannot be sensed with vision sense. This status is considered an advanced illusion, so magic vision cannot see past it.
Creatures that rely on sight can only notice and observe you with hearing and smell sense.
When creature only unprecisely senses you, every action against you is made with disadvantage, if they notice you with vague sense add another disadvantage.
Grappling or restraining creature gives ability to visualize where target could be enabling abilities and spells requiring precisely sensing and invisible gives then 1 less disadvantage to do actions against invisible.

actions.name: Disarmed
actions.longDescription:
Creature have 25% chance to fail somatic component (wastes only action not magic resource)
Disadvantage on all strikes, athletics, and all dexterity skill rolls

actions.name: Drained
actions.longDescription:
Drained status have number and its cumulative
Drained will reduce your maximum health by that number.
You reduce number of drained every long rest by your level number + con mod + other bonuses.

This status subtracts vigorous status first deleting both simultaneously and equally, because they collide, no matter how long they last, they ""burn"" eachother.
This status is related to **decay**

actions.name: Hasted
actions.longDescription:
- Creature have doubled movement
- Creature gains another main action or bonus action( can choose)
- Creature gains another interaction
- Creature have advantage on any dexterity related roll
- Creature gains +2 AC

After haste status ends you creature must roll DC 20 fortitude save two times or get {{dazzled}} status.
Hasted status overrides {{swift}} status. When you have this status it cancels itself with {{clumsy}} status making them both not relevant when both are active.
It also gains {{enfeebled}} status for one minute. Creature can repeat saving throw at the end of a turn.

actions.name: Confused
actions.longDescription:
A creature confused will have to roll 1d8
Confused creature speak fails to understand others.
Creature have disadvantage on perception rolls.
Creature will use {{opportunity strike}} on all occasions.
1-2 The creature uses all its movement to move in a random direction. To determine the direction, roll a d8 and assign a direction to each die face.
If it can it has to use {{tumble through}}.
3-6 The creature doesn’t move or take actions this turn.
7-8 The creature uses its whole turn to do most harm to random closest creature (from start of a turn)

Every time creature gets damage can repeat saving throw if possible. Does not work on poisons.

This status is related to **psychic damage**.

actions.name: Silenced
actions.longDescription: Verbal communication and verbal component for spell is blocked.

actions.name: Doomed
actions.longDescription:
Doomed status have number on it and its cumulative
A creature that is doomed will have less maximum wounded status equal to doomed status.
If doomed status will be equal to character maximum wounded status the creature will die on the spot.
If you die under doomed status all doomed status is removed.

## Creatures without wounded statuses
Creature will die if it has 10 life hit points or less per 1 doomed status

This status is related to **decay**

actions.name: Encumbered
actions.longDescription:
**If first stage encumbered:**
- You are {{clumsy}}

**If second stage encumbered:**
- You gain {{clumsy}} status
- No movement and jump is impossible
- You automatically fail reflex saves

actions.name: Stupefied
actions.longDescription:
Creature that is stupefied will have disadvantage on any wisdom, charisma and intelligence related roll.
Also stupefied creature will have 50% chance to fail casting spell wasting an appropriate action (not spellslots).

This status is related to **psychic damage**.

actions.name: Enfeebled
actions.longDescription:
Creature that is enfeebled will have disadvantage on any strength or constitution related roll.
Creature maximum bulk is cut in half (rounded down)
Creature deals half the damage from weapon damage or other athletics and physical interactions. (rounded down)
Your jumping power is cut in half (rounded down)

actions.name: Clumsy
actions.longDescription:
Creature that is clumsy will have disadvantage on reflex saves and any dexterity related roll.
You also don't take into account your dexterity when calculating AC
Your movement spending is doubled

actions.name: Unhealable
actions.longDescription:
You cannot gain life hit points.

This status is related to **decay**.

actions.name: Exhausted
actions.longDescription:
This status can stack, only one exhaustion stack is removed when you long rest
(Optional rule) All of exhaustion stacks are removed on long rest
This status grants:
- **I stack:** {{Doomed}} 1 status per exhausted status.
- **II stacks:** {{Tired}} status
- **III stacks:** You have hallucinations from time to time (flavour)

actions.name: Empowered
actions.longDescription:
Creature that is Empowered will have advantage on any strength or constitution related roll.
Creature half maximum bulk (rounded down) is added before any calculation is made.
Creature cannot deal less damage than average on weapon damage dices (rounded down)
Creature jump is doubled (rounded down)
When you have this status it cancels itself with {{enfeebled}} status making them both not relevant when both are active.

actions.name: Swift
actions.longDescription:
Creature that is swift will have advantage on reflex saving throws and any dexterity related roll.
Creature movement is doubled.
{{Opportunity strike}}s against you when you are not restrained or grappled are made with disadvantage.
When you have this status it cancels itself with {{clumsy}} status making them both not relevant when both are active.

actions.name: Enlightened
actions.longDescription:
Creature with enlightened status gains advantage on intelligence and wisdom check and saving throw, only exception is perception, insight and survival check that requires sense
When you have this status it cancels itself with {{stupefied}} status making them both not relevant when both are active.

actions.name: Perceptive
actions.longDescription:
Creature with perceptive status gains advantage on any perception, insight and survival check that requires sense.
Creature also is immune to any sense degradation, except blindness and deafness.

actions.name: Influential
actions.longDescription: Creature with influential status gains advantage on any charisma skill

actions.name: Vigorous
actions.longDescription:
Creature with vigorous status gains as much maximum life hit points as it has stacks of this status.
When you gain vigorous status only the highest amount gained counts, If you have already 10 and you gain 4 it does nothing.
This status subtracts {{drained}} status first deleting both simultaneously and equally, because they collide, no matter how long they last, they ""burn"" eachother.

actions.name: Tired
actions.longDescription:
You have disadvantage on everything until you finish long rest or short rest (depending on how tired you are)
You have additional disadvantage against effects that put you to sleep.

actions.name: Hidden
actions.longDescription:
While you are hidden creatures cannot target you (except aoe effects) and don't know where you are unless they will observe you.
When you are hidden you gain bonuses based on being noticed and unnoticed.
When you are noticed or unnoticed any reflex saving throw you force is made with disadvantage and strike or athletics roll you make is made with advantage.
When you are unnoticed to a creature you double all effects.
After you strike , cast a spell, do a harmful action you break stealth.
Stealing is not harmful action.

Creatures have to use seek action to break your stealth or just sense you clearly.

actions.name: Bleeding
actions.longDescription:
When you bleed you take indirect slashing damage on end of a turn. (damage always depends and should be listed).
Bleeding works only when creature can bleed. Bleeding will work only if creature is injured on its life hit points.
Bleeding does not stack and uses higher damage if presented.
To stop bleeding you need to use medicine check with dc equal to your stabilization dc or heal creature to the full.

actions.name: Burning
actions.longDescription:
When you burn you take indirect fire damage on end of a turn. (damage always depends and should be listed).
Burning does not stack and uses higher damage if presented.
To stop burning you need to get in complete water, spend an action to get prone and roll (using all of your maximum walking movement) or use item to spill water onto yourself.
Getting cold damage, being in very cold environment or being in very strong wind can douse flames to.
Anything that makes sense should work to.
Alternatively you can roll DC 20 fortitude saving throw at the end of a turn to get rid of this status.
When you burn you shed light 3/6

This status is related to **fire damage**

actions.name: Chilled
actions.longDescription:
When you get chilled you take indirect cold damage every time you take cold damage, but only once per round. (damage always depends and should be listed).
Chilled does not stack and uses higher damage if presented.
Chilled creature will have its speed reduced by half ( rounded up)
You get resistance to fire equal to 5
To stop this status you can take damage from fire, be around something very warm like lava or for 10 minutes around some campfire
Or it is specified in spell or ability.
Anything that makes sense should work to.
Alternatively you can roll DC 20 fortitude saving throw at the end of a turn to get rid of this status.

This status is related to **cold damage**

actions.name: Electrified
actions.longDescription:
(examples) This status is acquired when touching cables with energy or elemental grapples you
When you get electrified you take indirect electric damage on end of a turn. (damage always depends and should be listed).
Electrified does not stack and uses higher damage if presented.
You are also {{paralyzed}}, and can end effect at the end of a turn to attempt fortitude saving throw with disadvantage to cut yourself from source of energy (if possible)
To stop this status other you need to stop touching or getting touched by energy source. Pushing should work.
Be careful, grabbing electrified creature can make other creature electrified to.
Anything that makes sense should work.
Alternatively you can roll DC 20 fortitude saving throw at the end of a turn to get rid of this status.
Creatures immune to electric damage are immune to this status.

This status is related to **electric damage**

actions.name: Dissolving
actions.longDescription:
When you dissolve you take indirect acid damage on end of a turn. (damage always depends and should be listed).
Dissolving does not stack and uses higher damage if presented.
You get {{enfeebled}} status.
To stop this status other you need to submerge affecting bodypart in water or wait one minute (getting again status resets timer)
Alternatively you can roll DC 20 fortitude saving throw at the end of a turn to get rid of this status.

This status is related to **acid damage**

actions.name: Wet
actions.longDescription:
When you are wet you are vulnerable to cold and electric damage and have double disadvantage to anything related to cold and electric status.
You also have resistance to fire and acid damage equal to 5 and have advantage on anything related to acid or fire damage.
Getting any of this damages removes status unless you are in area giving this effect.
Wet characters with clothes gain +1 bulk encumbrance for any clothing,tent or backpack. Anything soaking water.

actions.name: Oiled
actions.longDescription:
When you are oiled you are vulnerable to fire damage and have disadvantages to any fire related roll. 
You also have resistance acid damage equal to 5 and have advantage to any acid related roll. 
Oiled creature depending on amount of oil will have its speed reduced by half ( rounded up) and cannot fly.
Getting fire damage gives {{burning}} status (5 fire damage).
While oiled you have 50/50% chance to extinguish yourself with rolling on ground and water extinguishes you only when completely submerged.
If you are oiled and you extinguish yourself from burning oiled is removed.
You need to wash all oil from you. It takes 10 minutes.

actions.name: Assailable
actions.longDescription:
You are either sleeping or taken hostage and because of life points and damage rulings a special rule is made for special moments of vulnerability like having gun to your head or blade to your throat. To get that status you have to be very defenceless.
This status can be given by {{unconscious}}, {{paralyzed}} or {{stunned}} status or by restraining or grappling creature and spending 1 action to enable this status for you to benefit. Every creature who wants to benefit from this status will have to spend that action and precisely sense it like with vision or touch.
Losing all those statuses or precise sense in some cases will free creature from such state.

In this state you get 2x more direct damage (stacks with critical hits)
Creatures that causes you to be assailable have advantage on their strikes against you.
